overall: Atlanta has seen an unusually flat overnight temperature profile, with the thermometer stuck at 77.0°F from midnight through 06:19 ET — zero warming velocity and zero acceleration. A high dewpoint of 73.4°F and a relatively low cloud ceiling (~457m with 62% cloud fraction) have suppressed any early-morning fluctuation. The atmosphere is loaded with moisture, which will both limit clear-sky solar forcing and set the stage for potential convective development as heating begins later this morning.
forecast_obs_notes: The three NWP models show a meaningful spread: NBM is the coolest at 81.9°F, ECMWF sits at 83.7°F, and HRRR is the most aggressive at 86.9°F — a roughly 5-degree range. The current observed temp of 77.0°F is fully consistent with a normal pre-dawn baseline given the season, so models are not yet being challenged by observations. HRRR's higher forecast likely reflects more robust afternoon mixing through the humid airmass, while NBM may be discounting peak heating due to cloud cover.
max_temp_prediction: The META model — the most reliable fused signal — places the highest probability in the 86–87°F bucket (26.4%), with meaningful probability extending into the 88–91°F range (~36% combined) and a long tail toward cooler outcomes driven by cloud/moisture uncertainty. Roughly 71% of META probability mass sits at or above 86°F, implying a clear lean toward the mid-to-upper 80s. Given the NWP model consensus (~84°F average, HRRR at 86.9°F), the high-humidity airmass that suppresses maximum solar heating, and scattered clouds that may partially break during the afternoon peak near 14h ET, the best single estimate is approximately 86.0°F with moderate-to-good confidence.
